extracted.intended_audience: Congressional staff, patent practitioners, industry stakeholders, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes the substantive legal and policy standards, procedural limits, and evaluative criteria contained in analysis of H.R. 1908 (Patent Reform Act of 2007), including willfulness, post-grant review, damages apportionment, PTO rulemaking, venue, and related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willful infringement standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A court may only find willful infringement if the patent owner shows, by clear and convincing evidence, that (1) the infringer, after receiving detailed written notice from the patentee, performed the acts of infringement, (2) the infringer intentionally copied the patented invention with knowledge that it was patented, or (3) after having been found by a court to have infringed a patent, the infringer engaged in conduct that again infringed on the same patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegation of willfulness is subject to a 'good faith' defense. The bill contains limitations intended to narrow circumstances in which willfulness findings (and thus enhanced damages) are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior user rights expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: H.R. 1908 expands the 'prior user rights' defense to infringement, where an earlier inventor began using a product or process (although unpatented) before another obtained a patent for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates a defensive right for entities with earlier commercial use to continue using the subject matter even after another obtains a patent, reducing exposure to infringement suits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single post-grant review opportunity within 12 months
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill establishes a single opportunity for challenge that must be initiated within 12 months of the patent being granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to cure deficiencies of reexamination procedures and to provide an efficient administrative mechanism for validity challenges while limiting repetitive or strategic filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant review abuse safeguards (discovery/improper use rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill requires the PTO Director to prescribe rules for abuse of discovery or improper use of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking authority is directed to define and curb abusive discovery practices or improper tactical uses of post-grant review to protect patentees from harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on types of prior art in post-grant review
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill 'limits the types of prior art which may be considered' in post-grant review proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricts the scope of prior art admissible in the administrative proceeding to reduce uncertainty and constrain broad validity attacks; text signals a narrower prior-art universe than open-court litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel/prohibition on reasserting claims litigated in post-grant review
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill 'prohibits a party from reasserting claims in court that it raised in post-grant review.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates estoppel to prevent duplicative litigation and to ensure finality of issues raised in the administrative challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue reform and forum-shopping limits
rubrics_metrics.description: H.R. 1908 would 'restore balance' by allowing cases to be brought in locales including where the defendant is incorporated or has its principal place of business or has committed a substantial portion of the acts of infringement and has a physical facility controlled by the defendant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to reduce extensive forum shopping by plaintiffs and to make venue symmetrical and balanced between parties; supports transfers and more neutral forums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory appeals for claim construction (Markman orders)
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill 'provides the Federal Circuit jurisdiction over interlocutory decisions, known as Markman orders, in which the district court construes the claims of a patent as a matter of law.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits early appellate review of claim construction to clarify issues earlier in litigation and potentially streamline or narrow disputed issues before trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve judicial flexibility in damages assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The courts must have flexibility in the assessment of damages; the bill's drafters urge avoiding binding the court with a prescribed mechanism and preserving judges' flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the bill proposes a framework for reasonable royalties, stakeholders urge language that leaves judges with discretion to accept or reject jury decisions and to craft remedies appropriate to case facts; avoid rigid statutory formulas that displace judicial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages: Reasonable royalty framework (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: An award based upon a reasonable royalty shall be determined in accordance with specific subsections; the court shall identify the factors relevant to the determination and the court or jury shall consider only those factors in making the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bill requires courts to identify and rely on only the relevant factors for a given case, and indicates the court should consider applicability of enumerated paragraphs when calculating a reasonable royalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages factor: Relationship of damages to contributions over prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: If an infringer shows evidence that features not covered by the claimed invention contribute economic value to the accused product or process, an analysis may be conducted to ensure that a reasonable royalty is applied only to that economic value properly attributable to the claimed invention. The court or jury may exclude economic value properly attributable to features not covered by the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages apportionment so that damages correspond to the incremental value of the claimed invention over the prior art rather than to the entire product value when non-claimed features contribute value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages factor: Entire market value rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claimant shows that the claimed invention is the predominant basis for market demand for a product or process that has a functional relationship with the claimed invention, damages may be based upon the entire market value of the products or processes involved that satisfy that demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves the ability to award damages based on the entire market value only when the patented feature drives demand (i.e., a predominant basis), limiting blanket application of the entire-market-value rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages factor: Combination inventions valuation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a combination product or process the elements of which are present individually in the prior art, the patentee may show that the economic value attributable to the infringing product includes the value of the additional function resulting from the combination, as well as the enhanced value, if any, of some or all of the prior art elements resulting from the combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows patentees of combination inventions to recover for the new value created by combining known elements, recognizing enhanced or synergistic value beyond prior-art components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages factor: Other factors (including marketplace licensing)
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining a reasonable royalty, the court may also consider, or direct the jury to consider, the terms of any nonexclusive marketplace licensing of the invention, where appropriate, as well as any other relevant factors under applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits consideration of licensing practices and other context-specific factors in reasonable royalty calculations; courts may tailor the factor set to the evidentiary record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking limits on PTO authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The existing rulemaking language in the bill is described as 'too expansive' and giving the PTO unparalleled authority; stakeholders urge following the Senate's lead to remove the PTO rulemaking provision from the House bill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates for legislative rather than broad administrative standard-setting; alternatives proposed include removing PTO's broad rulemaking authority or imposing constraints (e.g., 60-day delay and congressional review).

rubrics_metrics.name: 60-day delay and congressional review for PTO rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment requires a 60-day delay before PTO rules take effect so that Congress may have the opportunity to review these rules. If Congress finds the rule unacceptable, it may vote on a Joint Resolution of Disapproval nullifying the PTO's action; if Congress does nothing, the rule takes effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural check is proposed to ameliorate concerns that a bad PTO rule could harm innovation; provides time and mechanism for Congressional oversight while allowing rulemaking to proceed absent disapproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent diversion of PTO user fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Include language to prevent the diversion of fees collected by the PTO for general revenue purposes by cancelling the appropriations account for PTO fees and creating a new account in the U.S. Treasury for the fees to be deposited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures fee revenues are used for PTO operations (e.g., hiring examiners) to reduce backlog and speed examination; stakeholders tie fee retention to improved patent quality and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain applicant option to avoid publication (secrecy of applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment maintains the ability of patent applicants to keep their application from going public until action is taken by the patent office (non-publication option).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses concerns that mandatory publication would expose inventions to theft prior to patent grant; preserves applicant control over publication in some circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid duplicative challenges and increased cost of patent ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics assert that a post-grant review process 'will lead to duplicative challenges, resulting in an increase to the cost of patent ownership and significantly decreasing the enforceability, predictability and value of all patents.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This articulates an evaluative standard for assessing proposed post-grant procedures: measure whether they create duplicative proceedings and increased costs that undermine patent value and enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative balancing of industry interests
rubrics_metrics.description: The final version of patent reform must address the legitimate interests of manufacturing, biotech, and small inventors; the law should not favor one sector (e.g., high-tech) over others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy criterion for evaluating reforms: ensure reforms protect the diversity of economic sectors and do not inadvertently harm particular industries or small inventors' incentives.
